claim: Filoviruses such as Ebola and Marburg virus bud from the host membrane as enveloped virions.
source: Filoviruses such as Ebola and Marburg virus bud from the host membrane as enveloped virions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about filovirus biology.

claim: The budding process is achieved by the matrix protein VP40.
source: This process is achieved by the matrix protein VP40.
evidence: This is established knowledge about VP40 function.

claim: When expressed alone, VP40 induces budding of filamentous virus-like particles.
source: When expressed alone, VP40 induces budding of filamentous virus-like particles, suggesting that localization to the plasma membrane, oligomerization into a matrix layer, and generation of membrane curvature are intrinsic properties of VP40.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Localization to the plasma membrane, oligomerization into a matrix layer, and generation of membrane curvature are intrinsic properties of VP40.
source: When expressed alone, VP40 induces budding of filamentous virus-like particles, suggesting that localization to the plasma membrane, oligomerization into a matrix layer, and generation of membrane curvature are intrinsic properties of VP40.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that VP40 alone can induce VLP formation.

claim: There has been no direct information on the structure of VP40 matrix layers within viruses or virus-like particles prior to this study.
source: There has been no direct information on the structure of VP40 matrix layers within viruses or virus-like particles.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to the current work.

claim: VP40 dimers assemble extended chains via C-terminal domain interactions.
source: VP40 dimers assemble extended chains via C-terminal domain interactions.
evidence: This is supported by structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VP40 chains stack to form 2D matrix lattices below the membrane surface.
source: These chains stack to form 2D matrix lattices below the membrane surface.
evidence: This is supported by structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VP40 lattices form a patchwork assembly across the membrane.
source: These lattices form a patchwork assembly across the membrane and suggesting that assembly may begin at multiple points.
evidence: This is supported by structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VP40 assembly may begin at multiple points.
source: These lattices form a patchwork assembly across the membrane and suggesting that assembly may begin at multiple points.
evidence: This is inferred from the patchwork nature of the lattices.

claim: The filovirus family includes viruses such as Ebola, Marburg, and Sudan viruses that can cause hemorrhagic fever and severe disease.
source: The filovirus family includes viruses such as Ebola, Marburg, and Sudan viruses that can cause hemorrhagic fever and severe disease (Feldmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Filoviruses package their single-stranded negative-sense RNA genomes with viral proteins including nucleoprotein (NP), VP24 and VP35, into helical ribonucleoprotein assemblies called nucleocapsids (NCs).
source: Filoviruses package their single-stranded negative-sense RNA genomes with viral proteins including nucleoprotein (NP), VP24 and VP35, into helical ribonucleoprotein assemblies called nucleocapsids (NCs) (Huang et al., 2002; Noda et al., 2010; Wan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: NCs are recruited to the plasma membrane and bud from the host cells as enveloped virions with a characteristic filamentous morphology.
source: NCs are recruited to the plasma membrane and bud from the host cells as enveloped virions with a characteristic filamentous morphology from which the family takes its name (Geisbert and Jahrling, 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The filovirus matrix protein, VP40, binds to and concentrates at the plasma membrane of infected cells.
source: The filovirus matrix protein, VP40, binds to and concentrates at the plasma membrane of infected cells, where it can interact with components of the NC to promote envelopment, and where it drives formation of the filamentous virus particles.
evidence: This is established knowledge about VP40 function.

claim: VP40 can interact with components of the NC to promote envelopment.
source: The filovirus matrix protein, VP40, binds to and concentrates at the plasma membrane of infected cells, where it can interact with components of the NC to promote envelopment, and where it drives formation of the filamentous virus particles.
evidence: This is established knowledge about VP40 function.

claim: VP40 drives formation of the filamentous virus particles.
source: The filovirus matrix protein, VP40, binds to and concentrates at the plasma membrane of infected cells, where it can interact with components of the NC to promote envelopment, and where it drives formation of the filamentous virus particles.
evidence: This is established knowledge about VP40 function.

claim: VP40 is required for viral budding.
source: VP40 is required for viral budding, and expression of VP40 alone is sufficient to drive formation of filamentous virus-like particles (VLPs) containing a matrix layer and membrane envelope (Harty et al., 2000; Jasenosky et al., 2001; Noda et al., 2002; Timmins et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Expression of VP40 alone is sufficient to drive formation of filamentous virus-like particles (VLPs) containing a matrix layer and membrane envelope.
source: VP40 is required for viral budding, and expression of VP40 alone is sufficient to drive formation of filamentous virus-like particles (VLPs) containing a matrix layer and membrane envelope (Harty et al., 2000; Jasenosky et al., 2001; Noda et al., 2002; Timmins et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The morphology of VP40-only VLPs is similar to that of true virions but their diameter is smaller.
source: The morphology of these VLPs is similar to that of true virions but their diameter is smaller (Noda et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: When VP40 is co-expressed with NC components NP, VP24 and VP35, VLPs are produced which are almost indistinguishable from true virions.
source: When VP40 is co-expressed with NC components NP, VP24 and VP35, VLPs are produced which are almost indistinguishable from true virions (Bharat et al., 2012; Noda et al., 2005; Wan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A number of crystal structures have been determined of Ebola virus VP40 (eVP40) and Sudan (Ebola) virus (sVP40).
source: A number of crystal structures have been determined of Ebola virus VP40 (eVP40) and Sudan (Ebola) virus (sVP40) (Bornholdt et al., 2013; Clifton et al., 2015; Dessen et al., 2000; Gomis-Rüth et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: VP40 contains an N-terminal domain (NTD) and a C-terminal domain (CTD), linked by an intrasubunit hinge.
source: VP40 contains an N-terminal domain (NTD) and a C-terminal domain (CTD), linked by an intrasubunit hinge.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: Both eVP40 and sVP40 have been crystallized in space group C2 with similar unit cell dimensions.
source: Both eVP40 and sVP40 have been crystallized in space group C2 with similar unit cell dimensions.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: C2 crystals reveal dimers assembled via a hydrophobic interface in the NTD, involving residues A55, H61, F108, A113, M116, and L117 which are distributed across two alpha-helices (residues 52–65, 108–117).
source: These crystals reveal dimers assembled via a hydrophobic interface in the NTD, involving residues A55, H61, F108, A113, M116, and L117 which are distributed across two alpha-helices (residues 52–65, 108–117).
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: Disruption of the NTD dimer interface by site-directed mutagenesis prevents migration of VP40 to the plasma membrane and prevents matrix assembly.
source: Disruption of the NTD dimer interface by site-directed mutagenesis prevents migration of VP40 to the plasma membrane and prevents matrix assembly (Bornholdt et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Within the typical C2 crystal packing of unmodified VP40, eVP40, and sVP40 dimers are further arranged in linear assemblies via a hydrophobic CTD-CTD interface.
source: Within the typical C2 crystal packing of unmodified VP40, eVP40, and sVP40 dimers are further arranged in linear assemblies via a hydrophobic CTD-CTD interface (Bornholdt et al., 2013; Dessen et al., 2000; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and reference to a figure.

claim: The CTD-CTD interface involves residues L203, I237, M241, M305, and I307, which together form a relatively smooth hydrophobic patch.
source: This interface involves residues L203, I237, M241, M305, and I307, which together form a relatively smooth hydrophobic patch (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by reference to a figure.

claim: The CTD contains a basic patch composed of six lysine residues (K221, K224, K225, K270, K274, K275), which is essential for matrix assembly and membrane budding.
source: The CTD also contains a basic patch composed of six lysine residues (K221, K224, K225, K270,K274, K275), which is essential for matrix assembly and membrane budding (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by reference to a figure and established knowledge.

claim: A crystal structure of Marburg VP40 (mVP40) has been determined.
source: A crystal structure of Marburg VP40 (mVP40) has also been determined (Oda et al., 2016; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work and reference to a figure.

claim: eVP40 and mVP40 have 42% sequence identity and a C-alpha RMSD of 2.4 Å in the NTD.
source: eVP40 and mVP40 have 42% sequence identity and a C-alpha RMSD of 2.4 Å in the NTD, but only 16% sequence identity and 5.6 Å C-alpha RMSD in the CTD.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: eVP40 and mVP40 have only 16% sequence identity and 5.6 Å C-alpha RMSD in the CTD.
source: eVP40 and mVP40 have 42% sequence identity and a C-alpha RMSD of 2.4 Å in the NTD, but only 16% sequence identity and 5.6 Å C-alpha RMSD in the CTD.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: The overall topology of mVP40 is similar to that of eVP40.
source: The overall topology of mVP40, however, is similar to that of eVP40.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: The mVP40 monomer has similar N- and C-terminal domains, although there is a small rotation of the CTD relative to the NTD when compared to eVP40.
source: The mVP40 monomer has similar N- and C-terminal domains, although there is a small rotation of the CTD relative to the NTD when compared to eVP40.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: mVP40 dimerizes via an NTD interface that is very similar to that in eVP40.
source: mVP40 dimerizes via an NTD interface that is very similar to that in eVP40, and mVP40 also forms dimers in solution that are required for membrane binding and filament budding.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: mVP40 forms dimers in solution that are required for membrane binding and filament budding.
source: mVP40 dimerizes via an NTD interface that is very similar to that in eVP40, and mVP40 also forms dimers in solution that are required for membrane binding and filament budding.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: The mVP40 CTD basic patch is required for membrane binding but is larger and flatter than that in eVP40.
source: The mVP40 CTD basic patch is also required for membrane binding but is larger and flatter than that in eVP40.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: In the mVP40 crystal packing, the CTDs meet at an angle and do not form the more extensive hydrophobic interface observed in the C2 crystals of eVP40 and sVP40.
source: In the mVP40 crystal packing, the CTDs meet at an angle and do not form the more extensive hydrophobic interface observed in the C2 crystals of eVP40 and sVP40 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by reference to a figure and established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: Deletion or proteolysis of the C-terminus or C-terminal domain or incubation with urea drives oligomerization of the eVP40 NTD into RNA-binding octameric rings.
source: Deletion or proteolysis of the C-terminus or C-terminal domain or incubation with urea drives oligomerization of the eVP40 NTD into RNA-binding octameric rings (Bornholdt et al., 2013; Gomis-Rüth et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Octameric rings are likely to have a function during the viral lifecycle independent of matrix formation.
source: Subsequent work suggests that octameric rings are likely to have a function during the viral lifecycle independent of matrix formation (Bornholdt et al., 2013; Gomis-Rüth et al., 2003; Hoenen et al., 2005; Hoenen et al., 2010b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A crystal structure of eVP40 was determined in the presence of the negatively charged additive dextran sulfate.
source: In an effort to mimic membrane-associated electrostatic conditions, a crystal structure of eVP40 was determined in the presence of the negatively charged additive dextran sulfate (Bornholdt et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Under dextran sulfate conditions, eVP40 assembled into linear hexamers.
source: Under these conditions, eVP40 assembled into linear hexamers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) with unit distances approximately consistent with earlier, lower resolution tomographic analysis of the VP40 layer in Ebola and Marburg virions (Beniac et al., 2012; Bharat et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and reference to a figure.

claim: The unit distances in eVP40 linear hexamers are approximately consistent with earlier, lower resolution tomographic analysis of the VP40 layer in Ebola and Marburg virions.
source: Under these conditions, eVP40 assembled into linear hexamers (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) with unit distances approximately consistent with earlier, lower resolution tomographic analysis of the VP40 layer in Ebola and Marburg virions (Beniac et al., 2012; Bharat et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The core of the linear hexamer consists of four NTDs from which the linked CTDs are disordered or 'sprung' and not resolved.
source: The core of the linear hexamer consists of four NTDs from which the linked CTDs are disordered or 'sprung' and not resolved.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: The first and sixth VP40s in the hexamer retain their CTD in close association with its NTD.
source: The first and sixth VP40s in the hexamer retain their CTD in close association with its NTD.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: The CTDs of the first and sixth VP40s in the hexamer assemble into linear filaments via the same CTD-CTD interactions observed in the C2 crystals of VP40 dimers.
source: These CTDs assemble into linear filaments via the same CTD-CTD interactions observed in the C2 crystals of VP40 dimers.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: The NTD-NTD interfaces within the hexamer alternate between the dimer interface and the same NTD-NTD interface observed in the octameric ring.
source: The NTD-NTD interfaces within the hexamer alternate between the dimer interface and the same NTD-NTD interface observed in the octameric ring.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior structural studies.

claim: No linear hexamer structure has been determined for mVP40.
source: No linear hexamer structure has been determined for mVP40.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge.

claim: Mutagenesis of residues in mVP40 homologous to those forming the 'octamer-like' interfaces in hexameric eVP40 retains the ability of mVP40 to dimerize but prevents membrane binding and budding.
source: However, mutagenesis of residues in mVP40 homologous to those forming the 'octamer-like' interfaces in hexameric eVP40 (Bornholdt et al., 2013; Hoenen et al., 2010a) retains the ability of mVP40 to dimerize but prevents membrane binding and budding.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Based on existing data it seems likely that VP40 is arranged in a similar way in both MARV and EBOV particles.
source: Based on existing data it seems likely that VP40 is arranged in a similar way in both MARV and EBOV particles.
evidence: This is speculation based on prior data.

claim: The current model for the assembly state of VP40 within filovirus particles consists of VP40 hexamers as crystallized in the presence of dextran sulfate, arranged to form a 2D lattice.
source: The current model for the assembly state of VP40 within filovirus particles consists of VP40 hexamers as crystallized in the presence of dextran sulfate, arranged to form a 2D lattice, with dimensions of the 2D lattices in the model based upon repeating features observed in low-resolution cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) studies (Beniac et al., 2012; Bharat et al., 2011; Bornholdt et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The dimensions of the 2D lattices in the model are based upon repeating features observed in low-resolution cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) studies.
source: The current model for the assembly state of VP40 within filovirus particles consists of VP40 hexamers as crystallized in the presence of dextran sulfate, arranged to form a 2D lattice, with dimensions of the 2D lattices in the model based upon repeating features observed in low-resolution cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) studies (Beniac et al., 2012; Bharat et al., 2011; Bornholdt et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Analysis of transfected cells suggested that VP40 assembles into hexamers and octamers at the plasma membrane and in protrusions.
source: Analysis of transfected cells suggested that VP40 assembles into hexamers and octamers at the plasma membrane and in protrusions (Adu-Gyamfi et al., 2012) and that the interaction is mediated by the C-terminal domains (Adu-Gyamfi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The interaction of VP40 at the plasma membrane is mediated by the C-terminal domains.
source: Analysis of transfected cells suggested that VP40 assembles into hexamers and octamers at the plasma membrane and in protrusions (Adu-Gyamfi et al., 2012) and that the interaction is mediated by the C-terminal domains (Adu-Gyamfi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The structure and arrangement of VP40 within actual assembled virus particles is unknown prior to this study.
source: The structure and arrangement of VP40 within actual assembled virus particles, however, is unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to the current work.

claim: It remains unclear how VP40 assembles in the actual virion prior to this study.
source: It therefore remains unclear how VP40 assembles in the actual virion, which model of VP40 assembly best reflects that in the virion, and how VP40 induces membrane curvature and assembly with other viral components.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to the current work.

claim: It remains unclear which model of VP40 assembly best reflects that in the virion prior to this study.
source: It therefore remains unclear how VP40 assembles in the actual virion, which model of VP40 assembly best reflects that in the virion, and how VP40 induces membrane curvature and assembly with other viral components.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to the current work.

claim: It remains unclear how VP40 induces membrane curvature and assembly with other viral components prior to this study.
source: It therefore remains unclear how VP40 assembles in the actual virion, which model of VP40 assembly best reflects that in the virion, and how VP40 induces membrane curvature and assembly with other viral components.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to the current work.

claim: eVP40 and sVP40, with intact CTDs and in the absence of charged additives, consistently crystallize in linear filaments of dimers in the space group C2.
source: eVP40 and sVP40, with intact CTDs and in the absence of charged additives, consistently crystallize in linear filaments of dimers in the space group C2 (Bornholdt et al., 2013; Clifton et al., 2015; Dessen et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: eVP40 was crystallized in two alternate crystal forms: P62 and P6422.
source: In an attempt to determine if this linear arrangement is an inherent preferred assembly interface of eVP40 or simply the result of the common C2 crystal packing, we crystallized eVP40 in two alternate crystal forms: P62 and P6422.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In both P62 and P6422 crystal forms, eVP40 builds linear filaments of dimers, mediated by CTD-CTD interdimer interfaces, with CTD basic patches displayed on a common face.
source: Notably, in both of these crystal forms, eVP40 also builds linear filaments of dimers, mediated by CTD-CTD interdimer interfaces, with CTD basic patches displayed on a common face.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The P62 and P6422 filaments differ from the C2 filaments by slight torsional rotation about the relatively flat hydrophobic CTD-CTD interface.
source: These filaments differ from the C2 filaments by slight torsional rotation about the relatively flat hydrophobic CTD-CTD interface (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F and Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to a figure and table.

claim: The propensity of VP40 to form linear assemblies by CTD-CTD interactions across multiple crystal forms suggests this is a biologically preferred interface.
source: The propensity of VP40 to form linear assemblies by CTD-CTD interactions across multiple crystal forms suggest this is a biologically preferred interface and may be important in the viral particle or virus assembly.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of consistent linear assemblies across multiple crystal forms.

claim: The linear CTD-CTD interface may be important in the viral particle or virus assembly.
source: The propensity of VP40 to form linear assemblies by CTD-CTD interactions across multiple crystal forms suggest this is a biologically preferred interface and may be important in the viral particle or virus assembly.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation of consistent linear assemblies.

claim: eVP40 expression induces budding of long VLPs from the surface of mammalian cells.
source: eVP40 expression induces budding of long VLPs from the surface of mammalian cells (Noda et al., 2002; Timmins et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Purified Zaire eVP40 VLPs are multi-micron long filaments with a diameter of ~ 28 nm.
source: We purified Zaire eVP40 VLPs by sucrose gradient purification and imaged them by cryo-ET, finding multi-micron long filaments with a diameter of ~ 28 nm (Table 2) and a matrix-like protein layer visible under the membrane bilayer.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to a table.

claim: eVP40 VLPs have a matrix-like protein layer visible under the membrane bilayer.
source: We purified Zaire eVP40 VLPs by sucrose gradient purification and imaged them by cryo-ET, finding multi-micron long filaments with a diameter of ~ 28 nm (Table 2) and a matrix-like protein layer visible under the membrane bilayer.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The structure of the matrix layer in intact eVP40 VLPs was determined to a resolution of 10 Å.
source: We applied subtomogram averaging methods to determine the structure of the matrix layer to a resolution of 10 Å (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2) from intact eVP40 VLPs.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to figures.

claim: The matrix layer in eVP40 VLPs is formed by higher-order linear oligomerization of VP40 dimers on the inner surface of the viral membrane.
source: We observed that the matrix layer is formed by higher-order linear oligomerization of VP40 dimers on the inner surface of the viral membrane.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VP40 dimers in eVP40 VLPs form long chains that stack to form 2D lattices with a monoclinic p2 space group in the plane of the membrane.
source: VP40 dimers form long chains that stack to form 2D lattices with a monoclinic p2 space group in the plane of the membrane (Figure 1, Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to a figure and table.

claim: The crystal structure of the C2 eVP40 dimer (PDB: 4LDB) could be fit as a rigid body into the density of eVP40 VLPs.
source: The crystal structure of the C2 eVP40 dimer (PDB: 4LDB) could be fit as a rigid body into the density, showing that linear oligomerization is mediated by CTD to CTD interactions.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Linear oligomerization in eVP40 VLPs is mediated by CTD to CTD interactions.
source: The crystal structure of the C2 eVP40 dimer (PDB: 4LDB) could be fit as a rigid body into the density, showing that linear oligomerization is mediated by CTD to CTD interactions.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VLPs were produced by co-expression of eVP40 with the Ebola virus glycoprotein GP.
source: In addition to eVP40 VLPs, we also produced VLPs by co-expression of eVP40 with the Ebola virus glycoprotein GP, and by co-expression of eVP40 with the NC components NP, VP24 and VP35.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VLPs were produced by co-expression of eVP40 with the NC components NP, VP24 and VP35.
source: In addition to eVP40 VLPs, we also produced VLPs by co-expression of eVP40 with the Ebola virus glycoprotein GP, and by co-expression of eVP40 with the NC components NP, VP24 and VP35.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NP-VP24-VP35-VP40 VLPs have substantially wider filaments to accommodate the NC-like assembly.
source: As described previously (Bharat et al., 2012), NP-VP24-VP35-VP40 VLPs have substantially wider filaments to accommodate the NC-like assembly (Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work and reference to a table.

claim: The structures of eVP40 within VP40-GP VLPs and NP-VP24-VP35-VP40 VLPs were determined at resolutions of 10 Å.
source: We determined the structures of eVP40 within these VLPs at resolutions of 10 Å, (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to figures.

claim: The matrix layer in VP40-GP VLPs and NP-VP24-VP35-VP40 VLPs is formed from extended chains of eVP40 that stack to form monoclinic p2 lattices.
source: As in the eVP40 VLPs, the matrix layer in these VLPs is formed from extended chains of eVP40 that stack to form monoclinic p2 lattices (Figure 1, Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to a figure and table.

claim: The C2 crystallographic eVP40 dimer was fit as a rigid body into the matrix structures from all three VLPs.
source: We were able to fit the C2 crystallographic eVP40 dimer as a rigid body into the matrix structures from all three VLPs (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to a figure.

claim: No substantial electron density that is not occupied by eVP40 was observed in the VLP matrix structures.
source: We did not observe any substantial electron density that is not occupied by eVP40.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The eVP40 dimers in VLPs are oriented similarly such that the basic patches in the CTDs all point toward and contact the membrane.
source: The eVP40 dimers are oriented similarly such that the basic patches in the CTDs all point toward and contact the membrane.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The orientation of eVP40 dimers in VLPs is consistent with previous studies showing that mutations within the basic patch modulate membrane binding.
source: This orientation is consistent with previous studies, which showed that mutations within this patch modulate membrane binding (Bornholdt et al., 2013), and consistent with linear assemblies observed in crystals in which the basic patches are oriented in the same direction.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In all VLPs, oligomerization of eVP40 dimers to form extended chains occurs through a hydrophobic surface patch in the CTD.
source: In all VLPs, oligomerization of eVP40 dimers to form extended chains occurs through a hydrophobic surface patch in the CTD.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A hydrophobic CTD-CTD interaction is found in each of the C2, P62 and P6422 eVP40 and sVP40 crystal forms, with slightly varying orientations about the CTD-CTD interface.
source: A hydrophobic CTD-CTD interaction is also found in each of the C2, P62 and P6422 eVP40 and sVP40 crystal forms, with slightly varying orientations about the CTD-CTD interface (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to figures.

claim: The dimeric NTD-NTD interfaces are considered rigid.
source: In contrast to the flexible CTD-CTD interface, the dimeric NTD-NTD interfaces are considered rigid (Bornholdt et al., 2013), and are largely conserved in different crystal structures (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work and reference to a figure.

claim: The dimeric NTD-NTD interfaces are largely conserved in different crystal structures.
source: In contrast to the flexible CTD-CTD interface, the dimeric NTD-NTD interfaces are considered rigid (Bornholdt et al., 2013), and are largely conserved in different crystal structures (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to a figure.

claim: The flexibility about the CTD-CTD interfaces, and possibly also from the intrasubunit NTD-CTD hinge, appear sufficient to accommodate the varying radii of assembled matrix layers.
source: The flexibility about the CTD-CTD interfaces, and possibly also from the intrasubunit NTD-CTD hinge, appear sufficient to accommodate the varying radii of assembled matrix layers.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of varying lattice geometries.

claim: The CTD-CTD interface was probed by introducing either an M241R point mutation or an I307R mutation.
source: We previously probed the CTD-CTD interface by introducing either an M241R point mutation or an I307R mutation, both of which lie in the CTD-CTD interface.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: I307R was combined with R134A in the octameric assembly site to inhibit octamer formation.
source: I307R was combined with R134A in the octameric assembly site to inhibit octamer formation.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VP40 mutants bearing M241R or I307R substitutions do not assemble VLPs.
source: VP40 mutants bearing M241R or I307R substitutions do not assemble VLPs.
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: eVP40 bearing an M305F/I307F double mutation was generated.
source: We generated eVP40 bearing an M305F/I307F double mutation, which modeling studies suggested would support hydrophobic packing at the interface (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to a figure.

claim: Modeling studies suggested that M305F/I307F would support hydrophobic packing at the CTD-CTD interface.
source: We generated eVP40 bearing an M305F/I307F double mutation, which modeling studies suggested would support hydrophobic packing at the interface (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by data presented in the manuscript and reference to a figure.

claim: eVP40 M305F/I307F overall expressed to a lower yield.
source: Although eVP40 M305F/I307F overall expressed to a lower yield, the relative proportion of VLP budding was enhanced over wild-type (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
